Subject: New vendor onboarding — Order Form + downstream vendor details

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Parcelly is excited to get a sandbox account provisioned and move toward a signed Order Form. Before we route to procurement for signature, procurement has two asks related to downstream subcontractors:

1) A one-page list of any subprocessor changes (new vendors in the last 90 days) and whether they have SOC 2 or equivalent attestation.
2) A short description of where customer data flows (S3 region, any third-party log shipping, and whether PII leaves our VPC).

I've attached an initial Order Form with our edits (Parcelly_OrderForm_v2_redlines.docx) and a spreadsheet that the procurement team uses to capture evidence. Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide the subproc evidence matrix and whether legal will accept a redline with the standard DPA annex?

Also cc'ing Procurement who will own the DocuSign step.

Appreciate a quick sync — we are hoping to finalize by next Thursday.

Best,
Lena Rios
Head of Procurement
Parcelly Systems

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear list. Quick responses inline and a proposed next-steps checklist: 

- Subprocessor list: we can provide a scoped list for the Parcelly production stack (services that touch customer tokens/content). We will flag any vendors added in the last 90 days.
- Evidence: for most common infra vendors (AWS, GCP, S3 replication partners) we can provide SOC 2 attachments or a vendor attestation URL. For smaller third parties we can provide the standard lightweight questionnaire responses.
- Data flow summary: I'll attach a 1-page diagram + short text (S3 us-west-2 primary; event logs forwarded to our analytics partner in eu-west-1 only when customers opt-in). No PII leaves our VPC unless configured by the customer.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Legal quick sweep on the redlines (Kimberly) — accept/reject specific DPA language changes.
2) I provide the subproc matrix and dataflow note by EOD Wednesday (2026-12-03).
3) If legal asks for an amendment or additional evidence, we schedule a 30-min triage with Parcelly procurement Thurs morning.

Are you available Thu 12/4 10am PT for a short triage if needed?

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez

Redwood Inference

Mateo — quick legal notes to keep the review focused: 

1) Redlines: I skimmed Parcelly's edits. Most are standard commercial asks. We should not agree to perpetual data escrow access or broad crypto-key escrow clauses. We can accept the DPA annex with the following clarifications: limit subprocessor authorization to the current roster + 30-day notice for additions, and keep liability carveouts aligned with our MSA (no indemnity expansion).

2) Evidence: Provide SOC 2 + ISO links where available; for smaller subs provide the attestation matrix with completed questionnaire. Where we cannot share a third-party certificate, list the compensating controls and point to the relevant runbook.

3) Escrow/forensics: If Parcelly requests forensic access to logs beyond standard audit logs, we should scope that as a support engagement with defined audit windows.

Action for Mateo: send the subproc matrix and the one-page dataflow note. I will prepare a one-page legal summary we can share that says: "Redwood's standard subprocessor controls + evidence types." That should satisfy procurement in most cases. If Parcelly insists on contract language changes beyond the DPA annex, we escalate to procurement/legal director with a proposed concession list.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
